title: Order a league table by division, points and name

blocks.text: A chess club's league page lists every player in one table. Players are grouped by division, with the divisions in alphabetical order. Within a division the player with the most points comes first. Players on equal points are listed by name, so the table doesn't reshuffle every time the results feed refreshes and the players arrive in a different order.
`LeagueTable.sorted` already sorts with `standings()`. Write `standings()` in `src/main/java/practice/LeagueTable.java`. About three lines in total.

cases.says: within one division, players are listed from most points to fewest, and the input list is left alone
divisions run A to Z even though points run high to low, so reversing the order of points must not reverse the divisions
players on equal points are listed by name, whatever order they arrive in

origin.section: reversed() Reverses the Whole Comparator Chain Built Before It

concepts: reversed() on a chained comparator reverses every key in the chain; one key is reversed by giving its thenComparing a reverse-order comparator.
